<reason>CON opened by saying "only" defeats the motion, but under PRO's pressure questions conceded that every extension must be assessed across all three categories before approval, that transit shortfalls must be fixed before licensing, and that lapsing obligations should be extended as conditions. PRO effectively tracked that migration and showed CON's residual objection reduces to a single hypothetical venue whose already-enforceable plans get attached to the license at zero cost. PRO also supplied a workable measure for "stronger" (relative to what the current license obliges) that CON never displaced with a rival measure, and offered a concrete benefit of "only" (welding hours and plan so councils can't grant now and promise the bus later). CON argued cleanly and landed a real point that duplicating existing binding arrangements closes no gap, and correctly parried the transit-contradiction and 400-capacity examples. But a "closes no gap, costs nothing" objection is a thin basis to reject the motion, and PRO's closing made the choice easier to decide. PRO's two clipped turns are a genuine execution cost that keeps this from being a solid win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's A2 in Rebuttal 2: answering CON's demand for a concrete rejected extension with "nothing—because you have adopted the motion," then tracing CON's step-by-step convergence from "only defeats the motion" to "mandatory advance assessment," reframing the whole dispute as a quarrel over "stronger" in which CON had no rival measure.</best_rebuttal>
